# RESTORE.sh as tapectl 1.6.0 wrote it

`RESTORE-GOLD01-12.sh` is the RESTORE.sh (File 2) that tapectl v1.6.0 wrote
for a volume labelled `GOLD01` with 12 files: byte for byte the script whose
sha256 `tests/on_tape_golden.rs` pinned in 1.6.0
(`d9787a4ffdd05ba038416696d9866a9a285fc97509c35692a18dc3a9b68f9e9d`, `v1.6.0` on
`c9c5877`). It was generated by `generate_restore_script_v2("GOLD01", 12)` on
`p478-span` before any 1.7.0 change to RESTORE.sh, while that pin still held,
and checked against that hash.

`tests/heir_restore_sh.rs` runs it against tapes 1.7.0 writes, to prove ADR-0012
item 124: a span tape states `requires = ["short-seal", "spanning"]` in File 0,
and a 1.6.0 RESTORE.sh refuses it there by name, as a first and as a second
cartridge, while it still reads a 1.7.0 tape that does not span
(`volume-format-v2.md` §1.2). The test checks the hash first, so the fixture
cannot drift. Never edit the script: it is what an heir holding a tape written
by 1.6.0 has at its File 2.
